@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+name: Create Draft Release
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types:
+      - closed
+
+permissions: {}
+
+jobs:
+  create-draft-release:
+    if: >-
+      github.repository_owner == 'fastapi'
+      && github.event.pull_request.merged == true
+      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
+      && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release')
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    env:
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE: fastapi/__init__.py
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE: docs/en/docs/release-notes.md
+    steps:
+      - name: Dump GitHub context
+        env:
+          GITHUB_CONTEXT: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: echo "$GITHUB_CONTEXT"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          # The merge commit of the release PR
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merge_commit_sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
+        with:
+          python-version-file: ".python-version"
+      - name: Install uv
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
+        with:
+          # Before upgrading uv version, make sure astral-sh/setup-uv knows its checksum.
+          # See: https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/851#issuecomment-4282017837
+          version: "0.11.4"
+          enable-cache: false
+      - name: Extract release details
+        id: release-details
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="$(uv run --no-project --with "typer>=0.21.1" python scripts/prepare_release.py current-version)"
+          uv run --no-project --with "typer>=0.21.1" python scripts/prepare_release.py release-notes > draft-release-notes.md
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Create draft release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.release-details.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          gh release create "$VERSION" \
+            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+            --draft \
+            --title "$VERSION" \
+            --notes-file draft-release-notes.md \
+            --target "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

diff --git a/.github/workflows/prepare-release.yml b/.github/workflows/prepare-release.yml
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..e355a5341
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/prepare-release.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+name: Prepare Release
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      bump:
+        description: Release bump
+        required: true
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - patch
+          - minor
+          - major
+      date:
+        description: Release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.
+        required: false
+        type: string
+
+permissions: {}
+
+jobs:
+  prepare-release:
+    if: github.repository_owner == 'fastapi'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      issues: write
+      pull-requests: write
+    env:
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE: fastapi/__init__.py
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE: docs/en/docs/release-notes.md
+    steps:
+      - name: Dump GitHub context
+        env:
+          GITHUB_CONTEXT: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: echo "$GITHUB_CONTEXT"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          # Use a token that triggers other workflows (tests, labels) on the release PR
+          token: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_LATEST_CHANGES }} # zizmor: ignore[secrets-outside-env]
+          persist-credentials: true # Required for `git push` below
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
+        with:
+          python-version-file: ".python-version"
+      - name: Install uv
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
+        with:
+          # Before upgrading uv version, make sure astral-sh/setup-uv knows its checksum.
+          # See: https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/851#issuecomment-4282017837
+          version: "0.11.4"
+          enable-cache: false
+      - name: Prepare release
+        env:
+          PREPARE_RELEASE_BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump }}
+          PREPARE_RELEASE_DATE: ${{ inputs.date }}
+        run: uv run --no-project --with "typer>=0.21.1" python scripts/prepare_release.py prepare
+      - name: Get release version
+        id: release-version
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="$(uv run --no-project --with "typer>=0.21.1" python scripts/prepare_release.py current-version)"
+          echo "$version"
+          # Fail before opening the PR if the new release section has no changes
+          uv run --no-project --with "typer>=0.21.1" python scripts/prepare_release.py release-notes
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Create release pull request
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_LATEST_CHANGES }} # zizmor: ignore[secrets-outside-env]
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.release-version.outputs.version }}
+          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          branch="release-${VERSION}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}"
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git switch -c "$branch"
+          git add "$PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE" "$PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE"
+          git commit -m "🔖 Release version ${VERSION}"
+          git push --set-upstream origin "$branch"
+          gh pr create \
+            --base "$BASE_BRANCH" \
+            --head "$branch" \
+            --title "🔖 Release version ${VERSION}" \
+            --body "Prepare release ${VERSION}. Merging this PR creates a draft GitHub release; publishing that release publishes the package to PyPI." \
+            --label release

diff --git a/scripts/prepare_release.py b/scripts/prepare_release.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..3eb286401
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/prepare_release.py
@@ -0,0 +1,213 @@
+"""Prepare a release by updating the package version and release notes.
+
+Commands:
+
+* `prepare`: bump `__version__` and move the "Latest Changes" in the release
+  notes under a new dated version heading.
+* `current-version`: print the current `__version__`.
+* `release-notes`: print the release notes section for the current version.
+"""
+
+import re
+from datetime import date
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Annotated, Literal
+
+import typer
+
+DEFAULT_VERSION_FILE = Path("fastapi/__init__.py")
+DEFAULT_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE = Path("docs/en/docs/release-notes.md")
+
+VERSION_PATTERN = re.compile(r'(?m)^__version__ = "(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)"$')
+VERSION_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?m)^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)(?: \([^)]+\))?$")
+RELEASE_NOTES_HEADER = "# Release Notes\n\n"
+LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER = "## Latest Changes"
+BumpType = Literal["major", "minor", "patch"]
+
+app = typer.Typer()
+
+
+def parse_version(version: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", version):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid version: {version!r}. Expected format: X.Y.Z")
+    major, minor, patch = version.split(".")
+    return int(major), int(minor), int(patch)
+
+
+def get_current_version(content: str, version_file: Path) -> str:
+    matches = list(VERSION_PATTERN.finditer(content))
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Expected exactly one __version__ assignment in {version_file}, "
+            f"found {len(matches)}"
+        )
+    return matches[0].group(1)
+
+
+def bump_version(version: str, bump: BumpType) -> str:
+    major, minor, patch = parse_version(version)
+    if bump == "major":
+        return f"{major + 1}.0.0"
+    if bump == "minor":
+        return f"{major}.{minor + 1}.0"
+    if bump == "patch":
+        return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"
+    raise ValueError(f"Invalid bump: {bump!r}. Expected major, minor, or patch")
+
+
+def update_version_file(content: str, version: str, version_file: Path) -> str:
+    current_version = get_current_version(content, version_file)
+    if parse_version(version) <= parse_version(current_version):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"New version {version} must be greater than current version "
+            f"{current_version}"
+        )
+    return VERSION_PATTERN.sub(f'__version__ = "{version}"', content, count=1)
+
+
+def _version_heading(version: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
+    return re.compile(rf"(?m)^## {re.escape(version)}(?: \([^)]+\))?$")
+
+
+def update_release_notes(
+    content: str, version: str, release_date: date, release_notes_file: Path
+) -> str:
+    # The release notes may start with front matter (e.g. MkDocs `hide`
+    # options), so look for the headers instead of requiring them at the start
+    latest_header = f"{RELEASE_NOTES_HEADER}{LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER}\n"
+    if latest_header not in content:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{release_notes_file} must contain {latest_header!r} "
+            "at the top of the release notes"
+        )
+    if _version_heading(version).search(content):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Release notes already contain a section for {version}")
+
+    release_header = f"## {version} ({release_date.isoformat()})"
+    return content.replace(
+        latest_header,
+        f"{latest_header}\n{release_header}\n",
+        1,
+    )
+
+
+def get_release_notes_body(content: str, version: str, release_notes_file: Path) -> str:
+    match = _version_heading(version).search(content)
+    if not match:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Could not find release notes section for {version} in "
+            f"{release_notes_file}"
+        )
+
+    next_match = VERSION_HEADING_PATTERN.search(content, match.end())
+    end = next_match.start() if next_match else len(content)
+    body = content[match.end() : end].strip()
+    if not body:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Release notes section for {version} in {release_notes_file} is empty"
+        )
+    return f"{body}\n"
+
+
+VersionFileOption = Annotated[
+    Path,
+    typer.Option(
+        envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE",
+        exists=True,
+        file_okay=True,
+        dir_okay=False,
+        readable=True,
+        help="Path to the Python file containing the __version__ assignment.",
+    ),
+]
+
+ReleaseNotesFileOption = Annotated[
+    Path,
+    typer.Option(
+        envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE",
+        exists=True,
+        file_okay=True,
+        dir_okay=False,
+        readable=True,
+        help="Path to the release notes Markdown file.",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+@app.command()
+def prepare(
+    bump: Annotated[
+        BumpType,
+        typer.Argument(
+            envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_BUMP",
+            help="The release bump to make: major, minor, or patch.",
+        ),
+    ],
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = DEFAULT_VERSION_FILE,
+    release_notes_file: ReleaseNotesFileOption = DEFAULT_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE,
+    release_date: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        typer.Option(
+            "--date",
+            envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_DATE",
+            help="Release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.",
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Bump the version and add a dated release heading to the release notes."""
+    # An empty string (e.g. an unset workflow input) means today
+    parsed_release_date = (
+        date.fromisoformat(release_date) if release_date else date.today()
+    )
+
+    version_file_content = version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    release_notes_content = release_notes_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    version = bump_version(
+        get_current_version(version_file_content, version_file), bump
+    )
+
+    # Compute both new contents before writing anything, so that an error
+    # doesn't leave the files half updated
+    new_version_file_content = update_version_file(
+        version_file_content, version, version_file
+    )
+    new_release_notes_content = update_release_notes(
+        release_notes_content, version, parsed_release_date, release_notes_file
+    )
+    version_file.write_text(new_version_file_content, encoding="utf-8")
+    release_notes_file.write_text(new_release_notes_content, encoding="utf-8")
+
+    typer.echo(f"Prepared release {version} ({parsed_release_date.isoformat()})")
+
+
+@app.command()
+def current_version(
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = DEFAULT_VERSION_FILE,
+) -> None:
+    """Print the current version."""
+    typer.echo(
+        get_current_version(version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version_file)
+    )
+
+
+@app.command()
+def release_notes(
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = DEFAULT_VERSION_FILE,
+    release_notes_file: ReleaseNotesFileOption = DEFAULT_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE,
+) -> None:
+    """Print the release notes section for the current version."""
+    version = get_current_version(
+        version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version_file
+    )
+    typer.echo(
+        get_release_notes_body(
+            release_notes_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
+            version,
+            release_notes_file,
+        ),
+        nl=False,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    app()

diff --git a/docs/en/docs/tutorial/server-sent-events.md b/docs/en/docs/tutorial/server-sent-events.md

index 00000000..d5024bc4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/en/docs/tutorial/server-sent-events.md
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+# Server-Sent Events (SSE) { #server-sent-events-sse }
+
+You can stream data to the client using **Server-Sent Events** (SSE).
+
+This is similar to [Stream JSON Lines](stream-json-lines.md){.internal-link target=_blank}, but uses the `text/event-stream` format, which is supported natively by browsers with the [`EventSource` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventSource).
+
+/// info
+
+Added in FastAPI 0.135.0.
+
+///
+
+## What are Server-Sent Events? { #what-are-server-sent-events }
+
+SSE is a standard for streaming data from the server to the client over HTTP.
+
+Each event is a small text block with "fields" like `data`, `event`, `id`, and `retry`, separated by blank lines.
+
+It looks like this:
+
+```
+data: {"name": "Portal Gun", "price": 999.99}
+
+data: {"name": "Plumbus", "price": 32.99}
+
+```
+
+SSE is commonly used for AI chat streaming, live notifications, logs and observability, and other cases where the server pushes updates to the client.
+
+/// tip
+
+If you want to stream binary data, for example video or audio, check the advanced guide: [Stream Data](../advanced/stream-data.md).
+
+///
+
+## Stream SSE with FastAPI { #stream-sse-with-fastapi }
+
+To stream SSE with FastAPI, use `yield` in your *path operation function* and set `response_class=EventSourceResponse`.
+
+Import `EventSourceResponse` from `fastapi.sse`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[1:25] hl[4,22] *}
+
+Each yielded item is encoded as JSON and sent in the `data:` field of an SSE event.
+
+If you declare the return type as `AsyncIterable[Item]`, FastAPI will use it to **validate**, **document**, and **serialize** the data using Pydantic.
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[1:25] hl[10:12,23] *}
+
+/// tip
+
+As Pydantic will serialize it in the **Rust** side, you will get much higher **performance** than if you don't declare a return type.
+
+///
+
+### Non-async *path operation functions* { #non-async-path-operation-functions }
+
+You can also use regular `def` functions (without `async`), and use `yield` the same way.
+
+FastAPI will make sure it's run correctly so that it doesn't block the event loop.
+
+As in this case the function is not async, the right return type would be `Iterable[Item]`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[28:31] hl[29] *}
+
+### No Return Type { #no-return-type }
+
+You can also omit the return type. FastAPI will use the [`jsonable_encoder`](./encoder.md){.internal-link target=_blank} to convert the data and send it.
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[34:37] hl[35] *}
+
+## `ServerSentEvent` { #serversentevent }
+
+If you need to set SSE fields like `event`, `id`, `retry`, or `comment`, you can yield `ServerSentEvent` objects instead of plain data.
+
+Import `ServerSentEvent` from `fastapi.sse`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial002_py310.py hl[4,24,26] *}
+
+The `data` field is always encoded as JSON. You can pass any value that can be serialized as JSON, including Pydantic models.
+
+## Raw Data { #raw-data }
+
+If you need to send data **without** JSON encoding, use `raw_data` instead of `data`.
+
+This is useful for sending pre-formatted text, log lines, or special <dfn title="A value used to indicate a special condition or state">"sentinel"</dfn> values like `[DONE]`.
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial003_py310.py hl[17] *}
+
+/// note
+
+`data` and `raw_data` are mutually exclusive. You can only set one of them on each `ServerSentEvent`.
+
+///
+
+## Resuming with `Last-Event-ID` { #resuming-with-last-event-id }
+
+When a browser reconnects after a connection drop, it sends the last received `id` in the `Last-Event-ID` header.
+
+You can read it as a header parameter and use it to resume the stream from where the client left off:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial004_py310.py hl[25,27,31] *}
+
+## SSE with POST { #sse-with-post }
+
+SSE works with **any HTTP method**, not just `GET`.
+
+This is useful for protocols like [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) that stream SSE over `POST`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial005_py310.py hl[14] *}
+
+## Technical Details { #technical-details }
+
+FastAPI implements some SSE best practices out of the box.
+
+* Send a **"keep alive" `ping` comment** every 15 seconds when there hasn't been any message, to prevent some proxies from closing the connection, as suggested in the [HTML specification: Server-Sent Events](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#authoring-notes).
+* Set the `Cache-Control: no-cache` header to **prevent caching** of the stream.
+* Set a special header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to **prevent buffering** in some proxies like Nginx.
+
+You don't have to do anything about it, it works out of the box. 🤓

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable, Iterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel

+

+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def sse_items() -> AsyncIterable[Item]:
+    for item in items:

+def sse_items_no_async() -> Iterable[Item]:
+    for item in items:

+@app.get("/items/stream-no-annotation", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def sse_items_no_annotation():
+    for item in items:
+        yield item
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream-no-async-no-annotation", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+def sse_items_no_async_no_annotation():
+    for item in items:

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+from typing import Annotated
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Header
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Item(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    price: float
+
+
+items = [
+    Item(name="Plumbus", price=32.99),
+    Item(name="Portal Gun", price=999.99),
+    Item(name="Meeseeks Box", price=49.99),
+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def stream_items(
+    last_event_id: Annotated[int | None, Header()] = None,
+) -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent]:
+    start = last_event_id + 1 if last_event_id is not None else 0
+    for i, item in enumerate(items):
+        if i < start:
+            continue
+        yield ServerSentEvent(data=item, id=str(i))

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Prompt(BaseModel):
+    text: str
+
+
+@app.post("/chat/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def stream_chat(prompt: Prompt) -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent]:
+    words = prompt.text.split()

+from typing import Annotated, Any
+
+from annotated_doc import Doc
+from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, Field, model_validator
+from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse
+
+# Canonical SSE event schema matching the OpenAPI 3.2 spec
+# (Section 4.14.4 "Special Considerations for Server-Sent Events")
+_SSE_EVENT_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
+    "type": "object",
+    "properties": {
+        "data": {"type": "string"},
+        "event": {"type": "string"},
+        "id": {"type": "string"},
+        "retry": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0},
+    },
+}
+
+
+class EventSourceResponse(StreamingResponse):
+    """
+    Streaming response with `text/event-stream` media type.
+
+    Use as `response_class=EventSourceResponse` on a *path operation* that uses
+    `yield` to enable Server Sent Events (SSE) responses.
+
+    Works with **any HTTP method** (`GET`, `POST`, etc.), which makes it
+    compatible with protocols like MCP that stream SSE over `POST`.
+
+    The actual encoding logic lives in the FastAPI routing layer. This class
+    serves mainly as a marker and sets the correct `Content-Type`.
+
+    ## Example
+
+    ```python
+    from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+    from fastapi import FastAPI
+    from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse
+
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+
+    @app.get("/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+    async def stream() -> AsyncIterable[dict]:
+        yield {"message": "hello"}
+    ```
+    """
+
+    media_type = "text/event-stream"
+
+
+def _check_id_no_null(v: str | None) -> str | None:
+    if v is not None and "\0" in v:
+        raise ValueError("SSE 'id' must not contain null characters")
+    return v
+
+
+class ServerSentEvent(BaseModel):
+    """
+    Represents a single Server-Sent Event.
+
+    When `yield`ed from a *path operation function* that uses
+    `response_class=EventSourceResponse`, each `ServerSentEvent` is encoded
+    into the [SSE wire format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream)
+    (`text/event-stream`).
+
+    If you yield a plain object (dict, Pydantic model, etc.) instead, it is
+    automatically JSON-encoded and sent as the `data:` field.
+
+    All `data` values **including plain strings** are JSON-serialized.
+
+    For example, `data="hello"` produces `data: "hello"` on the wire (with
+    quotes). Use `raw_data` to send a string without JSON encoding.
+    """
+
+    data: Annotated[
+        Any,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            The event payload.
+
+            Can be any JSON-serializable value: a Pydantic model, dict, list,
+            string, number, etc. It is **always** serialized to JSON: strings
+            are quoted (`"hello"` becomes `data: "hello"` on the wire).
+
+            Mutually exclusive with `raw_data`.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    raw_data: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Raw string to send as the `data:` field **without** JSON encoding.
+
+            Use this when you need to send pre-formatted text, HTML fragments,
+            CSV lines, or any non-JSON payload. The string is placed directly
+            into the `data:` field as-is.
+
+            Mutually exclusive with `data`.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    event: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event type name.
+
+            Maps to `addEventListener(event, ...)` on the browser. When omitted,
+            the browser dispatches on the generic `message` event.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    id: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        AfterValidator(_check_id_no_null),
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event ID.
+
+            The browser sends this value back as the `Last-Event-ID` header on
+            automatic reconnection. **Must not contain null (`\\0`) characters.**
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    retry: Annotated[
+        int | None,
+        Field(ge=0),
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional reconnection time in **milliseconds**.
+
+            Tells the browser how long to wait before reconnecting after the
+            connection is lost. Must be a non-negative integer.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    comment: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional comment line(s).
+
+            Comment lines start with `:` in the SSE wire format and are ignored
+            by `EventSource` clients. Useful for keep-alive pings to prevent
+            proxy/load-balancer timeouts.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+
+    @model_validator(mode="after")
+    def _check_data_exclusive(self) -> "ServerSentEvent":
+        if self.data is not None and self.raw_data is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Cannot set both 'data' and 'raw_data' on the same "
+                "ServerSentEvent. Use 'data' for JSON-serialized payloads "
+                "or 'raw_data' for pre-formatted strings."
+            )
+        return self
+
+
+def format_sse_event(
+    *,
+    data_str: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Pre-serialized data string to use as the `data:` field. Multi-line
+            strings are split into multiple `data:` lines.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+    event: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc("Optional event type name (`event:` field)."),
+    ] = None,
+    id: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc("Optional event ID (`id:` field)."),
+    ] = None,
+    retry: Annotated[
+        int | None,
+        Doc("Optional reconnection time in milliseconds (`retry:` field)."),
+    ] = None,
+    comment: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc("Optional comment line(s) (lines starting with `:`)."),
+    ] = None,
+) -> bytes:
+    """
+    Build SSE wire-format bytes from **pre-serialized** data.
+
+    The result always ends with `\\n\\n` (the event terminator).
+    """
+    lines: list[str] = []
+
+    if comment is not None:
+        for line in comment.splitlines() or [""]:
+            lines.append(f": {line}")
+
+    if event is not None:
+        lines.append(f"event: {event}")
+
+    if data_str is not None:
+        for line in data_str.splitlines() or [""]:
+            lines.append(f"data: {line}")
+
+    if id is not None:
+        lines.append(f"id: {id}")
+
+    if retry is not None:
+        lines.append(f"retry: {retry}")
+
+    lines.append("")
+    lines.append("")
+    return "\n".join(lines).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+# Keep-alive comment, per the SSE spec recommendation
+KEEPALIVE_COMMENT = b": ping\n\n"
+
+# Seconds between keep-alive pings when a generator is idle.
+# Private but importable so tests can monkeypatch it.
+_PING_INTERVAL: float = 15.0

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+# Vibe Coding { #vibe-coding }
+
+Sometimes you don't want to decide up front which HTTP method a *path operation* uses or what shape its body has. You just want to vibe. ✨
+
+For that, use `@app.vibe()` (or `@router.vibe()` on an `APIRouter`).
+
+## Use `@app.vibe()` { #use-app-vibe }
+
+{* ../../docs_src/vibe/tutorial001_py310.py hl[9] *}
+
+This *path operation*:
+
+* Accepts **any** HTTP method: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `HEAD`, and `TRACE`.
+* Accepts **any** request body. A parameter named `body` with no explicit `Body()`, `Query()`, `Depends()`, etc. receives the whole request body. If the client sends no body, it is `None`, unless you set a different default.
+* Can still declare path, query, header, cookie parameters and dependencies, as with any other *path operation*.
+
+## The `prompt` { #the-prompt }
+
+You can pass a `prompt` describing what the *path operation* is supposed to do. It is included in the OpenAPI schema of each generated operation under the `x-vibe-prompt` extension.
+
+/// tip
+
+Each HTTP method is registered as its own *path operation*, so the OpenAPI schema and the docs UI show one entry per method, each with its own operation ID.
+
+///

+def _vibe_endpoint(func: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
+    """
+    Return an endpoint for `func` where a plain `body` parameter receives the
+    whole request body (any JSON, or nothing at all), instead of being read as
+    a query parameter.

+    Parameters that already declare how to be read (e.g. `Body()`, `Query()`,
+    `Depends()`, or `Annotated[...]`) are left untouched, and so is `func`
+    itself: a wrapper with an adjusted signature is returned.
+    """

+    param = signature.parameters.get("body")
+    if (
+        param is None
+        or param.kind
+        in (inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL, inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD)
+        or isinstance(param.default, (params.Param, params.Body, params.Depends))
+        or get_origin(param.annotation) is Annotated
+        or (isinstance(param.annotation, str) and "Annotated" in param.annotation)
+    ):

+    default = None if param.default is inspect.Parameter.empty else param.default

+    # parameter keyword-only keeps the signature valid now that `body` has a
+    # default, no matter where it is declared.
+    new_params = [

+        if p.kind is not inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD
+        else p
+        for p in signature.parameters.values()
+        if p.kind is not inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL
+    ]
+    new_params = [
+        p.replace(default=params.Body(default=default)) if p.name == "body" else p
+        for p in new_params
+    ]

+    def endpoint(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
+        return func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    endpoint.__signature__ = signature.replace(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+        parameters=new_params
+    )
+    return endpoint

+## Stream JSON Lines
+
+To stream data that can be structured as JSON, use `yield` in the *path operation function* and declare the return type as `AsyncIterable[Item]` (or `Iterable[Item]` for regular `def` functions). FastAPI will send it as JSON Lines (`application/jsonl`), validating, documenting, and serializing each item with Pydantic.
+
+```python
+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Item(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    description: str | None
+
+
+items = [
+    Item(name="Plumbus", description="A multi-purpose household device."),
+    Item(name="Portal Gun", description="A portal opening device."),
+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream")
+async def stream_items() -> AsyncIterable[Item]:
+    for item in items:
+        yield item
+```
+
+## Stream Data
+
+To stream pure binary data or strings, use `response_class=StreamingResponse` (or a subclass with a custom `media_type`) and `yield` in the *path operation function*, instead of creating and returning a `StreamingResponse` directly.
+
+```python
+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class PNGStreamingResponse(StreamingResponse):
+    media_type = "image/png"
+
+
+@app.get("/image/stream", response_class=PNGStreamingResponse)
+async def stream_image() -> AsyncIterable[bytes]:
+    for chunk in read_image():
+        yield chunk
+```
+
+instead of:
+
+```python
+# DO NOT DO THIS
+@app.get("/image/stream")
+async def stream_image():
+    async def generate():
+        for chunk in read_image():
+            yield chunk
+
+    return StreamingResponse(generate(), media_type="image/png")
+```
+
+If the data comes from a blocking source (e.g. a regular file), use a regular `def` function so it's run in a threadpool.
+
 ## Including Routers
 
 When declaring routers, prefer to add router level parameters like prefix, tags, etc. to the router itself, instead of in `include_router()`.

+from contextlib import AsyncExitStack

+

+# Used mainly to close files after the request is done, dependencies are closed
+# in their own AsyncExitStack
+class AsyncExitStackMiddleware:
+    def __init__(
+        self, app: ASGIApp, context_name: str = "fastapi_middleware_astack"
+    ) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+        self.context_name = context_name
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
+            scope[self.context_name] = stack
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)

+"""
+Access point for the (optional) Pydantic v1 compatibility layer.
+
+When Pydantic v2 is installed, Pydantic v1 functionality lives under
+`pydantic.v1`. Starting with Python 3.14, Pydantic (>= 2.12) no longer supports
+`pydantic.v1` and emits a warning as soon as it is imported. FastAPI should not
+trigger that warning by itself just because it is installed: the warning should
+only be shown if the user's own code imports `pydantic.v1`.
+
+So, on Python 3.14+ with Pydantic v2, this module exposes dummy placeholder
+classes instead of importing anything from `pydantic.v1`. Nothing can ever be an
+instance or subclass of these placeholders, so all the internal `isinstance()`
+and `issubclass()` checks for Pydantic v1 objects are simply `False`.
+
+In every other case, the real Pydantic v1 compatibility objects are exposed from
+`fastapi._compat.v1`.
+
+Internal code should import `may_v1` for these checks instead of `v1`, and only
+import `fastapi._compat.v1` lazily, when actually handling Pydantic v1 objects.
+"""
+
+import sys
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple, Union
+
+from pydantic.version import VERSION as PYDANTIC_VERSION
+
+_PYDANTIC_V2 = PYDANTIC_VERSION.startswith("2.")
+
+# TODO: remove when dropping support for Pydantic v1
+PYDANTIC_V1_AVAILABLE = not (_PYDANTIC_V2 and sys.version_info >= (3, 14))
+

+    # Pydantic v1 is not supported (and importing it emits a warning), expose
+    # placeholder classes that nothing will ever be an instance or subclass of.
+
+    class AnyUrl:
+        pass
+
+    class BaseConfig:
+        pass
+
+    class BaseModel:
+        pass
+
+    class Color:
+        pass
+
+    class ErrorWrapper:
+        pass
+
+    class FieldInfo:
+        def __init__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+            pass
+
+    class ModelField:
+        pass
+
+    class NameEmail:
+        pass
+
+    class SecretBytes:
+        pass
+
+    class SecretStr:
+        pass
+
+    class UndefinedType:
+        def __repr__(self) -> str:
+            return "PydanticV1Undefined"
+
+    Undefined = UndefinedType()
+
+    Url = AnyUrl
+
+    GetJsonSchemaHandler = Any
+    JsonSchemaValue = Dict[str, Any]
+    CoreSchema = Any
+

+    # shadowing typing.Required.

+
+    def _normalize_errors(errors: Sequence[Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        use_errors: List[Any] = []

+            else:

+    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:

+            {**err, "loc": loc_prefix + err.get("loc", ())}
+            for err in _normalize_errors(errors)
+        ]
+        return updated_loc_errors
+
+    def get_definitions(
+        *,
+        fields: List[ModelField],
+        model_name_map: Dict[Any, str],
+        separate_input_output_schemas: bool = True,
+    ) -> Tuple[Dict[Any, JsonSchemaValue], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
+        return {}, {}

+# Frontend { #frontend }
+
+If you have a frontend, for example a single page application (SPA) built with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, etc. you can serve its built files directly from your **FastAPI** app with `app.frontend()`.
+
+## Use `app.frontend()` { #use-app-frontend }
+
+Build your frontend, normally that would create a directory like `dist` with an `index.html` file and some other files (JavaScript, CSS, images, etc.).
+
+Then pass the path where you want to serve it and the `directory` with the files:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/frontend/tutorial001_py310.py hl[5] *}
+
+Now:
+
+* `/` will serve `dist/index.html`.
+* Existing files are served directly, for example `/assets/app.js` would serve `dist/assets/app.js`.
+* Any other `GET` request for a path without a file extension, for example `/users/42`, will also serve `dist/index.html`, so that the frontend (in the browser) can handle that route.
+* A missing file with an extension, for example `/assets/missing.js`, will return a `404` error instead of the `index.html`.
+
+## Path Operations First { #path-operations-first }
+
+The frontend has the **lowest priority**. Your *path operations* (and any other route) always take precedence, even if they are declared after `app.frontend()`.
+
+In the example above, `/api/items` is handled by the *path operation* function, and everything else that is not matched by any other route is handled by the frontend.
+
+Only `GET` and `HEAD` requests are handled by the frontend, other methods that don't match any route still return a `404` error.
+
+## Frontend in an `APIRouter` { #frontend-in-an-apirouter }
+
+You can also use `router.frontend()` in an `APIRouter`, the router prefix is applied to it as with any other route:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/frontend/tutorial002_py310.py hl[6,14] *}
+
+Here the frontend is served at `/admin`, and `/admin/api/users` is handled by the *path operation*.
+
+If there are several frontends that could handle a request, the one with the longest path is used. So, you could serve a main frontend at `/` and another one at `/admin`.
+
+## Details { #details }
+
+`app.frontend()` uses `StaticFiles` underneath, see [Static Files](../tutorial/static-files.md).
+
+You can pass a `name` to generate URLs for files in the frontend, for example with `request.url_for("frontend", path="/assets/app.js")`.
+
+By default, it checks that the directory exists when you call `app.frontend()`, raising an error if it doesn't. You can disable that check with `check_dir=False`, for example to declare it before building the frontend, it will then be checked when handling the first request to the frontend.

+name: Prepare Release
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      bump:
+        description: "Version bump: major, minor, patch, or an explicit version X.Y.Z"
+        required: true
+        default: patch
+
+permissions: {}
+
+jobs:
+  prepare-release:
+    if: github.repository_owner == 'fastapi'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Dump GitHub context
+        env:
+          GITHUB_CONTEXT: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: echo "$GITHUB_CONTEXT"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: true # Required for `git push` below
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
+        with:
+          python-version-file: ".python-version"
+      - name: Prepare release
+        id: prepare
+        env:
+          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump }}
+        run: python scripts/prepare_release.py "$BUMP"
+      - name: Create pull request
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.version }}
+          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+        run: |
+          branch="release/$VERSION"
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git switch -c "$branch"
+          git add fastapi/__init__.py docs/en/docs/release-notes.md
+          git commit -m "🔖 Release version $VERSION"
+          git push origin "$branch"
+          gh pr create \
+            --base "$BASE_BRANCH" \
+            --head "$branch" \
+            --title "🔖 Release version $VERSION" \
+            --body "Prepare release $VERSION: bump the version in \`fastapi/__init__.py\` and add the release header in the release notes."
diff --git a/scripts/prepare_release.py b/scripts/prepare_release.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..17e2f30c8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/prepare_release.py
@@ -0,0 +1,179 @@
+"""Prepare a new release.
+
+Bump the version in `fastapi/__init__.py` and move the "Latest Changes" in
+`docs/en/docs/release-notes.md` under a new header for the new version, with
+today's date.
+
+Usage:
+
+    python scripts/prepare_release.py patch
+    python scripts/prepare_release.py minor
+    python scripts/prepare_release.py major
+    python scripts/prepare_release.py 0.200.0
+
+The new version is printed to stdout, and when running in GitHub Actions, it's
+also written to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` as `version`.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+from datetime import date
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+VERSION_FILE = ROOT_DIR / "fastapi" / "__init__.py"
+RELEASE_NOTES_FILE = ROOT_DIR / "docs" / "en" / "docs" / "release-notes.md"
+
+LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER = "## Latest Changes"
+
+VERSION_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$")
+VERSION_LINE_PATTERN = re.compile(
+    r'^__version__ = "(?P<version>[^"]+)"', flags=re.MULTILINE
+)
+RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\b", flags=re.MULTILINE)
+
+
+class ReleaseError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def parse_version(version: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    match = VERSION_PATTERN.match(version)
+    if not match:
+        raise ReleaseError(f"Invalid version: {version!r}, expected X.Y.Z")
+    major, minor, patch = (int(part) for part in match.groups())
+    return major, minor, patch
+
+
+def bump_version(current_version: str, bump: str) -> str:
+    """Compute the new version from the current one.
+
+    `bump` is either one of `major`, `minor`, `patch`, or an explicit `X.Y.Z`
+    version, that has to be greater than the current one.
+    """
+    major, minor, patch = parse_version(current_version)
+    if bump == "major":
+        return f"{major + 1}.0.0"
+    if bump == "minor":
+        return f"{major}.{minor + 1}.0"
+    if bump == "patch":
+        return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"
+    if parse_version(bump) <= (major, minor, patch):
+        raise ReleaseError(
+            f"New version {bump} must be greater than current version {current_version}"
+        )
+    return bump
+
+
+def get_current_version(version_file_content: str) -> str:
+    match = VERSION_LINE_PATTERN.search(version_file_content)
+    if not match:
+        raise ReleaseError("Could not find __version__ in version file")
+    return match.group("version")
+
+
+def update_version_file(version_file_content: str, new_version: str) -> str:
+    # Validate that there's a version to replace
+    get_current_version(version_file_content)
+    return VERSION_LINE_PATTERN.sub(
+        f'__version__ = "{new_version}"', version_file_content, count=1
+    )
+
+
+def update_release_notes(
+    release_notes_content: str, new_version: str, release_date: date
+) -> str:
+    """Add a release header under "Latest Changes" for the new version.
+
+    The changes listed under "Latest Changes" end up under the new release
+    header, and "Latest Changes" is left empty, ready for the next changes.
+    """
+    lines = release_notes_content.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    header_indexes = [
+        i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.rstrip() == LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER
+    ]
+    if len(header_indexes) != 1:
+        raise ReleaseError(
+            f"Expected exactly one {LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER!r} header in release "
+            f"notes, found {len(header_indexes)}"
+        )
+    latest_index = header_indexes[0]
+
+    # The section ends at the next level 2 header
+    end_index = len(lines)
+    for i in range(latest_index + 1, len(lines)):
+        if lines[i].startswith("## "):
+            end_index = i
+            break
+
+    section_lines = lines[latest_index + 1 : end_index]
+    if not "".join(section_lines).strip():
+        raise ReleaseError(f"No changes found under {LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER!r}")
+
+    existing_versions = RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN.findall(release_notes_content)
+    if new_version in existing_versions:
+        raise ReleaseError(f"Release {new_version} already exists in release notes")
+
+    # Keep the line endings used by the file
+    newline = "\r\n" if lines[latest_index].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
+    new_header = f"## {new_version} ({release_date.isoformat()}){newline}"
+    new_lines = [
+        *lines[: latest_index + 1],
+        newline,
+        new_header,
+        *section_lines,
+        *lines[end_index:],
+    ]
+    return "".join(new_lines)
+
+
+def prepare_release(
+    bump: str,
+    *,
+    version_file: Path = VERSION_FILE,
+    release_notes_file: Path = RELEASE_NOTES_FILE,
+    release_date: date | None = None,
+) -> str:
+    """Update the version file and the release notes, return the new version."""
+    release_date = release_date or date.today()
+    version_content = version_file.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
+    release_notes_content = release_notes_file.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
+
+    current_version = get_current_version(version_content)
+    new_version = bump_version(current_version, bump)
+
+    # Compute everything before writing, so that nothing is written on errors
+    new_version_content = update_version_file(version_content, new_version)
+    new_release_notes_content = update_release_notes(
+        release_notes_content, new_version, release_date
+    )
+
+    version_file.write_bytes(new_version_content.encode("utf-8"))
+    release_notes_file.write_bytes(new_release_notes_content.encode("utf-8"))
+    return new_version
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "bump",

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# Vibe Coding { #vibe-coding }
+
+Are you tired of all that **data validation**, **documentation**, **serialization**, and all that **boring** stuff?
+
+Do you just want to **vibe**? 🎶
+
+**FastAPI** now supports a new `@app.vibe()` decorator that embraces modern AI coding best practices. 🤖
+
+## How It Works { #how-it-works }
+
+The `@app.vibe()` decorator is intended to receive **any HTTP method** (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, etc.) and **any payload**.
+
+The body should be annotated with `Any`, because the request and the response would be... well... **anything**. 🤷
+
+The idea is that you would receive the payload and send it **directly** to an LLM provider, using a `prompt` to tell the LLM what to do, and return the response **as is**. No questions asked.
+
+You don't even need to write the body of the function. The `@app.vibe()` decorator does everything for you based on AI vibes:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/vibe/tutorial001_py310.py hl[8:12] *}
+
+## Benefits { #benefits }
+
+By using `@app.vibe()`, you get to enjoy:
+
+* **Freedom**: No data validation. No schemas. Just vibes. ✨
+* **Flexibility**: The request and the response can be anything. You don't need to know what they are.
+* **No Documentation**: Why document your API when an LLM can figure it out? Automatic OpenAPI documentation is *so* 2018.
+* **No Serialization**: Just pass the raw, unstructured data around. Serialization is for people who don't trust their LLMs.
+* **Embrace Modern AI Coding Practices**: Leave all the decisions up to an LLM. What could go wrong? 🔥
+
+Stop overthinking and just vibe. 🎶
+
+## Nah { #nah }
+
+...or not. 😅
+
+If you try to use `@app.vibe()`, you will get an error:
+
+```
+fastapi.exceptions.FastAPIError: Are you kidding me? Happy April Fool's 🤡
+```
+
+**FastAPI** is all about **data validation**, **serialization**, and **automatic documentation**, based on standard Python type hints. Those things are what make your APIs **reliable**, **predictable**, and **easy to use**, for humans and for LLMs alike. 🤓
+
+So, enjoy coding with FastAPI the normal way. 😎

+### Dependencies with `yield`, `StreamingResponse`, Technical Details { #dependencies-with-yield-streamingresponse-technical-details }
+
+Since FastAPI 0.118.0, the exit code in dependencies with `yield` is executed *after* the response is done, this includes sending a `StreamingResponse` and running background tasks.
+
+This way you can use the resources from dependencies with `yield` (for example a database session) while streaming the content of a `StreamingResponse`, and uploaded files (`UploadFile`) are only closed after the response is done.
+
+Exceptions raised in the *path operation*, including `HTTPException`, are still passed to the dependencies with `yield` before the exception handlers run, so you can still catch them with `except` in those dependencies.

@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
+
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+
+# Used mainly to close files after the request is done, dependencies are closed
+# in their own AsyncExitStack
+class AsyncExitStackMiddleware:
+    def __init__(
+        self, app: ASGIApp, context_name: str = "fastapi_middleware_astack"
+    ) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+        self.context_name = context_name
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
+            scope[self.context_name] = stack
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)

+name: Create Draft Release
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types:
+      - closed
+
+permissions: {}
+
+jobs:

+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    env:
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE: fastapi/__init__.py
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE: docs/en/docs/release-notes.md
+    steps:
+      - name: Dump GitHub context
+        env:
+          GITHUB_CONTEXT: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: echo "$GITHUB_CONTEXT"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
+        with:
+          python-version-file: ".python-version"
+      - name: Install uv
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0

+          # See: https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/851#issuecomment-4282017837
+          version: "0.11.4"
+          enable-cache: "false"
+      - name: Extract release details
+        id: release-details
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="$(uv run --no-project --with typer python scripts/prepare_release.py current-version)"
+          uv run --no-project --with typer python scripts/prepare_release.py release-notes > draft-release-notes.md
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Create draft release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.release-details.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          gh release create "$VERSION" \
+            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+            --draft \
+            --title "$VERSION" \
+            --notes-file draft-release-notes.md \
+            --target "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

+name: Prepare Release
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      bump:
+        description: Release bump
+        required: true
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - patch
+          - minor
+          - major
+      date:
+        description: Release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.
+        required: false

+

+  prepare-release:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      issues: write
+      pull-requests: write
+    env:
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE: fastapi/__init__.py
+      PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE: docs/en/docs/release-notes.md
+    steps:
+      - name: Dump GitHub context
+        env:
+          GITHUB_CONTEXT: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: echo "$GITHUB_CONTEXT"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          token: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_LATEST_CHANGES }} # zizmor: ignore[secrets-outside-env]
+          persist-credentials: true
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
+        with:
+          python-version-file: ".python-version"
+      - name: Install uv
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
+        with:
+          # Before upgrading uv version, make sure astral-sh/setup-uv knows its checksum.
+          # See: https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/851#issuecomment-4282017837
+          version: "0.11.4"
+          enable-cache: "false"
+      - name: Prepare release
+        env:
+          PREPARE_RELEASE_BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump }}
+          PREPARE_RELEASE_DATE: ${{ inputs.date }}
+        run: uv run --no-project --with typer python scripts/prepare_release.py prepare
+      - name: Get release version
+        id: release-version
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="$(uv run --no-project --with typer python scripts/prepare_release.py current-version)"
+          echo "$version"
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Create release pull request
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_LATEST_CHANGES }} # zizmor: ignore[secrets-outside-env]
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.release-version.outputs.version }}
+          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          branch="release-${VERSION}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}"
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git switch -c "$branch"
+          git add "$PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE" "$PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE"
+          git commit -m "🔖 Release version ${VERSION}"
+          git push --set-upstream origin "$branch"
+          gh pr create \
+            --base "$BASE_BRANCH" \
+            --head "$branch" \
+            --title "🔖 Release version ${VERSION}" \
+            --body "Prepare release ${VERSION}." \
+            --label release

@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+"""Prepare a release by updating the package version and release notes."""
+
+import re
+from datetime import date
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Annotated, Literal
+
+import typer
+
+VERSION_PATTERN = re.compile(r'(?m)^__version__ = "(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)"$')
+VERSION_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?m)^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)(?: \([^)]+\))?[ \t]*$")
+FRONT_MATTER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\A---\n.*?\n---\n\n?", re.DOTALL)
+RELEASE_NOTES_HEADER = "# Release Notes\n\n"
+LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER = "## Latest Changes"
+BumpType = Literal["major", "minor", "patch"]
+
+app = typer.Typer()
+
+
+def parse_version(version: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", version):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid version: {version!r}. Expected format: X.Y.Z")
+    major, minor, patch = version.split(".")
+    return int(major), int(minor), int(patch)
+
+
+def get_current_version(content: str, version_file: Path) -> str:
+    matches = list(VERSION_PATTERN.finditer(content))
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Expected exactly one __version__ assignment in {version_file}, "
+            f"found {len(matches)}"
+        )
+    return matches[0].group(1)
+
+
+def bump_version(version: str, bump: BumpType) -> str:
+    major, minor, patch = parse_version(version)
+    if bump == "major":
+        return f"{major + 1}.0.0"
+    if bump == "minor":
+        return f"{major}.{minor + 1}.0"
+    if bump == "patch":
+        return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"
+    raise ValueError(f"Invalid bump: {bump!r}. Expected: major, minor, or patch")
+
+
+def update_version_file(content: str, version: str, version_file: Path) -> str:
+    current_version = get_current_version(content, version_file)
+    if parse_version(version) <= parse_version(current_version):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"New version {version} must be greater than current version "
+            f"{current_version}"
+        )
+    return VERSION_PATTERN.sub(f'__version__ = "{version}"', content, count=1)
+
+
+def _version_heading(version: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
+    return re.compile(rf"(?m)^## {re.escape(version)}(?: \([^)]+\))?[ \t]*$")
+
+
+def update_release_notes(
+    content: str, version: str, release_date: date, release_notes_file: Path
+) -> str:
+    # The release notes file may start with YAML front matter (e.g. for MkDocs)
+    front_matter_match = FRONT_MATTER_PATTERN.match(content)
+    front_matter = front_matter_match.group(0) if front_matter_match else ""
+    body = content[len(front_matter) :]
+
+    latest_header = f"{RELEASE_NOTES_HEADER}{LATEST_CHANGES_HEADER}\n"
+    if not body.startswith(latest_header):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{release_notes_file} must start with {latest_header!r} "
+            "(optionally after front matter)"
+        )
+    if _version_heading(version).search(body):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Release notes already contain a section for {version}")
+
+    release_header = f"## {version} ({release_date.isoformat()})"
+    new_body = f"{latest_header}\n{release_header}\n" + body[len(latest_header) :]
+    return front_matter + new_body
+
+
+def get_release_notes_body(content: str, version: str, release_notes_file: Path) -> str:
+    match = _version_heading(version).search(content)
+    if not match:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Could not find release notes section for {version} in "
+            f"{release_notes_file}"
+        )
+
+    next_match = VERSION_HEADING_PATTERN.search(content, match.end())
+    end = next_match.start() if next_match else len(content)
+    body = content[match.end() : end].strip()
+    if not body:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Release notes section for {version} in {release_notes_file} is empty"
+        )
+    return f"{body}\n"
+
+
+VersionFileOption = Annotated[
+    Path,
+    typer.Option(
+        envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE",
+        exists=True,
+        file_okay=True,
+        dir_okay=False,
+        readable=True,
+        help="Path to the Python file containing the __version__ assignment.",
+    ),
+]
+ReleaseNotesFileOption = Annotated[
+    Path,
+    typer.Option(
+        envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_RELEASE_NOTES_FILE",
+        exists=True,
+        file_okay=True,
+        dir_okay=False,
+        readable=True,
+        help="Path to the release notes Markdown file.",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+@app.command()
+def prepare(
+    bump: Annotated[
+        BumpType,
+        typer.Argument(
+            envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_BUMP",
+            help="The release bump to make: major, minor, or patch.",
+        ),
+    ],
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = Path("fastapi/__init__.py"),
+    release_notes_file: ReleaseNotesFileOption = Path("docs/en/docs/release-notes.md"),
+    release_date: Annotated[
+        str,
+        typer.Option(
+            "--date",
+            envvar="PREPARE_RELEASE_DATE",
+            help="Release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.",
+        ),
+    ] = "",
+) -> None:
+    """Bump the version and move the latest changes into a new release section."""
+    parsed_release_date = (
+        date.fromisoformat(release_date) if release_date else date.today()
+    )
+
+    version_file_content = version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    release_notes_content = release_notes_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    version = bump_version(
+        get_current_version(version_file_content, version_file), bump
+    )
+
+    # Compute both updates before writing anything, so a failure leaves no
+    # partially prepared release behind
+    new_version_file_content = update_version_file(
+        version_file_content, version, version_file
+    )
+    new_release_notes_content = update_release_notes(
+        release_notes_content, version, parsed_release_date, release_notes_file
+    )
+    version_file.write_text(new_version_file_content, encoding="utf-8")
+    release_notes_file.write_text(new_release_notes_content, encoding="utf-8")
+
+    typer.echo(f"Prepared release {version} ({parsed_release_date.isoformat()})")
+
+
+@app.command()
+def current_version(
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = Path("fastapi/__init__.py"),
+) -> None:
+    """Print the current package version."""
+    typer.echo(
+        get_current_version(version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version_file)
+    )
+
+
+@app.command()
+def release_notes(
+    version_file: VersionFileOption = Path("fastapi/__init__.py"),
+    release_notes_file: ReleaseNotesFileOption = Path("docs/en/docs/release-notes.md"),
+) -> None:
+    """Print the release notes section for the current version."""
+    version = get_current_version(
+        version_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version_file
+    )
+    typer.echo(
+        get_release_notes_body(
+            release_notes_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
+            version,
+            release_notes_file,
+        ),
+        nl=False,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    app()

+# Server-Sent Events (SSE) { #server-sent-events-sse }
+
+You can stream data to the client using **Server-Sent Events** (SSE).
+
+This is similar to [Stream JSON Lines](stream-json-lines.md){.internal-link target=_blank}, but uses the `text/event-stream` format, which is supported natively by browsers with the [`EventSource` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventSource).
+
+/// info
+
+Added in FastAPI 0.135.0.
+
+///
+
+## What are Server-Sent Events? { #what-are-server-sent-events }
+
+SSE is a standard for streaming data from the server to the client over HTTP.
+
+Each event is a small text block with "fields" like `data`, `event`, `id`, and `retry`, separated by blank lines.
+
+It looks like this:
+
+```
+data: {"name": "Portal Gun", "price": 999.99}
+
+data: {"name": "Plumbus", "price": 32.99}
+
+```
+
+SSE is commonly used for AI chat streaming, live notifications, logs and observability, and other cases where the server pushes updates to the client.
+
+/// tip
+
+If you want to stream binary data, for example video or audio, check the advanced guide: [Stream Data](../advanced/stream-data.md){.internal-link target=_blank}.
+
+///
+
+## Stream SSE with FastAPI { #stream-sse-with-fastapi }
+
+To stream SSE with FastAPI, use `yield` in your *path operation function* and set `response_class=EventSourceResponse`.
+
+Import `EventSourceResponse` from `fastapi.sse`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[1:25] hl[4,22] *}
+
+Each yielded item is encoded as JSON and sent in the `data:` field of an SSE event.
+
+If you declare the return type as `AsyncIterable[Item]`, FastAPI will use it to **validate**, **document**, and **serialize** the data using Pydantic.
+
+/// tip
+
+As Pydantic will serialize it in the **Rust** side, you will get much higher **performance** than if you don't declare a return type.
+
+///
+
+### Non-async *path operation functions* { #non-async-path-operation-functions }
+
+You can also use regular `def` functions (without `async`), and use `yield` the same way.
+
+FastAPI will make sure it's run correctly so that it doesn't block the event loop.
+
+As in this case the function is not async, the right return type would be `Iterable[Item]`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[28:31] hl[29] *}
+
+### No Return Type { #no-return-type }
+
+You can also omit the return type. FastAPI will use the `jsonable_encoder` to convert the data and send it.
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial001_py310.py ln[34:37] hl[35] *}
+
+## `ServerSentEvent` { #serversentevent }
+
+If you need to set SSE fields like `event`, `id`, `retry`, or `comment`, you can yield `ServerSentEvent` objects instead of plain data.
+
+Import `ServerSentEvent` from `fastapi.sse`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial002_py310.py hl[4,26] *}
+
+The `data` field is always encoded as JSON. You can pass any value that can be serialized as JSON, including Pydantic models.
+
+## Raw Data { #raw-data }
+
+If you need to send data **without** JSON encoding, use `raw_data` instead of `data`.
+
+This is useful for sending pre-formatted text, log lines, or special "sentinel" values like `[DONE]`.
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial003_py310.py hl[17] *}
+
+/// note
+
+`data` and `raw_data` are mutually exclusive. You can only set one of them on each `ServerSentEvent`.
+
+///
+
+## Resuming with `Last-Event-ID` { #resuming-with-last-event-id }
+
+When a browser reconnects after a connection drop, it sends the last received `id` in the `Last-Event-ID` header.
+
+You can read it as a header parameter and use it to resume the stream from where the client left off:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial004_py310.py hl[25,27,31] *}
+
+## SSE with POST { #sse-with-post }
+
+SSE works with **any HTTP method**, not just `GET`.
+
+This is useful for protocols like [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) that stream SSE over `POST`:
+
+{* ../../docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial005_py310.py hl[14] *}
+
+## Technical Details { #technical-details }
+
+FastAPI implements some SSE best practices out of the box.
+
+* Send a **"keep alive" `ping` comment** every 15 seconds when there hasn't been any message, to prevent some proxies from closing the connection, as suggested in the [HTML specification: Server-Sent Events](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#authoring-notes).
+* Set the `Cache-Control: no-cache` header to **prevent caching** of the stream.
+* Set a special header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to **prevent buffering** in some proxies like Nginx.
+
+You don't have to do anything about it, it works out of the box. 🤓

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable, Iterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Item(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    description: str | None
+
+
+items = [
+    Item(name="Plumbus", description="A multi-purpose household device."),
+    Item(name="Portal Gun", description="A portal opening device."),
+    Item(name="Meeseeks Box", description="A box that summons a Meeseeks."),
+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def sse_items() -> AsyncIterable[Item]:
+    for item in items:
+        yield item
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream-no-async", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+def sse_items_no_async() -> Iterable[Item]:
+    for item in items:
+        yield item
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream-no-annotation", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def sse_items_no_annotation():
+    for item in items:
+        yield item
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream-no-async-no-annotation", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+def sse_items_no_async_no_annotation():
+    for item in items:
+        yield item

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Item(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    price: float
+
+
+items = [

+    Item(name="Portal Gun", price=999.99),
+    Item(name="Meeseeks Box", price=49.99),
+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def stream_items() -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent]:
+    yield ServerSentEvent(comment="stream of item updates")

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+from typing import Annotated
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Header
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Item(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    price: float
+
+
+items = [
+    Item(name="Plumbus", price=32.99),
+    Item(name="Portal Gun", price=999.99),
+    Item(name="Meeseeks Box", price=49.99),
+]
+
+
+@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def stream_items(
+    last_event_id: Annotated[int | None, Header()] = None,
+) -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent]:
+    start = last_event_id + 1 if last_event_id is not None else 0
+    for i, item in enumerate(items):
+        if i < start:
+            continue
+        yield ServerSentEvent(data=item, id=str(i))

+from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+app = FastAPI()
+
+
+class Prompt(BaseModel):
+    text: str
+
+
+@app.post("/chat/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
+async def stream_chat(prompt: Prompt) -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent]:
+    words = prompt.text.split()
+    for word in words:
+        yield ServerSentEvent(data=word, event="token")
+    yield ServerSentEvent(raw_data="[DONE]", event="done")

+++ b/fastapi/sse.py
@@ -0,0 +1,228 @@
+from typing import Annotated, Any
+
+from annotated_doc import Doc
+from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, Field, model_validator
+from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse
+
+# Canonical SSE event schema matching the OpenAPI 3.2 spec
+# (Section 4.14.4 "Special Considerations for Server-Sent Events")
+_SSE_EVENT_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
+    "type": "object",
+    "properties": {
+        "data": {"type": "string"},
+        "event": {"type": "string"},
+        "id": {"type": "string"},
+        "retry": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0},
+    },
+}
+
+
+class EventSourceResponse(StreamingResponse):
+    """Streaming response with `text/event-stream` media type.
+
+    Use as `response_class=EventSourceResponse` on a *path operation* that uses
+    `yield` to enable Server Sent Events (SSE) responses.
+
+    Works with **any HTTP method** (`GET`, `POST`, etc.), which makes it compatible
+    with protocols like MCP that stream SSE over `POST`.
+
+    The actual encoding logic lives in the FastAPI routing layer. This class
+    serves mainly as a marker and sets the correct `Content-Type`.
+    """
+
+    media_type = "text/event-stream"
+
+
+def _check_id_no_null(v: str | None) -> str | None:
+    if v is not None and "\0" in v:
+        raise ValueError("SSE 'id' must not contain null characters")
+    return v
+
+
+class ServerSentEvent(BaseModel):
+    """Represents a single Server-Sent Event.
+
+    When `yield`ed from a *path operation function* that uses
+    `response_class=EventSourceResponse`, each `ServerSentEvent` is encoded
+    into the [SSE wire format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation)
+    (`text/event-stream`).
+
+    If you yield a plain object (dict, Pydantic model, etc.) instead, it is
+    automatically JSON-encoded and sent as the `data:` field.
+
+    All `data` values **including plain strings** are JSON-serialized.
+
+    For example, `data="hello"` produces `data: "hello"` on the wire (with
+    quotes). Use `raw_data` to send a string as-is, without JSON encoding.
+    """
+
+    data: Annotated[
+        Any,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            The event payload.
+
+            Can be any JSON-serializable value: a Pydantic model, dict, list,
+            string, number, etc. It is **always** serialized to JSON: strings
+            are quoted (`"hello"` becomes `data: "hello"` on the wire).
+
+            Mutually exclusive with `raw_data`.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    raw_data: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Raw string to send as the `data:` field **without** JSON encoding.
+
+            Use this when you need to send pre-formatted text, HTML fragments,
+            CSV lines, or any non-JSON payload. The string is placed directly
+            into the `data:` field as-is.
+
+            Mutually exclusive with `data`.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    event: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event type name.
+
+            Maps to `addEventListener(event, ...)` on the browser. When omitted,
+            the browser dispatches on the generic `message` event.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    id: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        AfterValidator(_check_id_no_null),
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event ID.
+
+            The browser sends this value back as the `Last-Event-ID` header on
+            automatic reconnection. **Must not contain null (`\\0`) characters.**
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    retry: Annotated[
+        int | None,
+        Field(ge=0),
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional reconnection time in **milliseconds**.
+
+            Tells the browser how long to wait before reconnecting after the
+            connection is lost. Must be a non-negative integer.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+    comment: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional comment line(s).
+
+            Comment lines start with `:` in the SSE wire format and are ignored by
+            `EventSource` clients. Useful for keep-alive pings to prevent
+            proxy/load-balancer timeouts.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None
+
+    @model_validator(mode="after")
+    def _check_data_exclusive(self) -> "ServerSentEvent":
+        if self.data is not None and self.raw_data is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Cannot set both 'data' and 'raw_data' on the same "
+                "ServerSentEvent. Use 'data' for JSON-serialized payloads "
+                "or 'raw_data' for pre-formatted strings."
+            )
+        return self
+
+
+def format_sse_event(
+    *,
+    data_str: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Pre-serialized data string to use as the `data:` field.
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+    event: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event type name (`event:` field).
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+    id: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional event ID (`id:` field).
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+    retry: Annotated[
+        int | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional reconnection time in milliseconds (`retry:` field).
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+    comment: Annotated[
+        str | None,
+        Doc(
+            """
+            Optional comment line(s) (`:` prefix).
+            """
+        ),
+    ] = None,
+) -> bytes:
+    """Build SSE wire-format bytes from **pre-serialized** data.
+
+    The result always ends with `\\n\\n` (the event terminator).
+    """
+    lines: list[str] = []
+
+    if comment is not None:
+        for line in comment.splitlines() or [""]:
+            lines.append(f": {line}")
+
+    if event is not None:
+        lines.append(f"event: {_single_line(event)}")
+
+    if data_str is not None:
+        for line in data_str.splitlines() or [""]:
+            lines.append(f"data: {line}")
+
+    if id is not None:
+        lines.append(f"id: {_single_line(id)}")
+
+    if retry is not None:
+        lines.append(f"retry: {retry}")
+
+    lines.append("")
+    lines.append("")
+    return "\n".join(lines).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+def _single_line(value: str) -> str:
+    # Field values for `event` and `id` can't contain line breaks, they would
+    # break the SSE framing
+    return value.replace("\r\n", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")
+
+
+# Keep-alive comment, per the SSE spec recommendation
+KEEPALIVE_COMMENT = b": ping\n\n"
+
+# Seconds between keep-alive pings when a generator is idle.
+# Private but importable so tests can monkeypatch it.
+_PING_INTERVAL: float = 15.0
